prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Draw a personable, detailed scientific cartoon of four selected receptor families answering "Where can the signal reach?". Target native 1024 x 1536 portrait. Warm rounded large molecular objects, restrained hand-painted texture, calm contours, very clear boundaries. No panels/cards or wall of text. Essential labels 44–48px at 1024px width; concise direct labels. Heading 64px. Intended display width 326–358 CSS px.

Critical correction: ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT HORIZONTAL PLASMA MEMBRANE at y=500, spanning the FULL WIDTH of the canvas. Its two leaflets have heads facing outside (above) and cytoplasm (below), tails toward each other. Do NOT curve it, do NOT draw any second plasma membrane anywhere, do NOT draw a cell outline or side wall. This is a magnified cell-edge cutaway. Everything below the band, including nucleus and internal receptor, is INSIDE the same cell; everything above is OUTSIDE. Label "Outside" above the band near the far right; "Inside" below the band near the right; "Cell membrane" directly along a clear membrane segment.

Three large surface receptors left-to-right span the SAME membrane at x=270, x=530, x=820. Their family headings are above their extracellular binding domains. Left heading "Ion channel": blue gated channel with obvious central pore and an extracellular coral ligand touching a binding site on the SIDE of the protein, NOT clogging its ion pore. Three violet charged ion beads and one downward arrow pass through its pore in an illustrative open state. Under it label "Ion flow". Middle heading "GPCR": slate-blue multipass receptor with ligand touching an outside pocket, then rounded three-part G protein clearly touching the receptor's CYTOPLASMIC end below the bilayer, with short inside-only arrow to it; label "G protein". Do NOT draw extracellular ligand crossing the GPCR. Right heading "Enzyme-linked" (split into two lines if needed): two ochre single-pass receptor chains, extracellular binding ends, each chain physically connected through the bilayer to its own cytoplasmic kinase domain. Short inside-only arrow from the enzyme domains to one small substrate bearing a "P" badge. Label "Kinase example" underneath. All three proteins are inserted in the bilayer, which continues between them. No arrows from these examples to growth, disease or treatment benefit.

Access comparison on the far LEFT near x=70, separate from channel. At y=240 draw one large outside probe with a short attempted inward path that STOPS exactly at the TOP of the plasma membrane with a blunt bar. Label "Stays outside" in two lines. Another physically distinct small diamond ligand at y=420 has a separate thin dashed path crossing the SAME PLASMA MEMBRANE at x=70 into cytoplasm at y=600. Label "Can enter" below this path. The probe stays entirely outside; the diamond's origin is unmistakably outside and destination unmistakably inside. These paths must not merge; they do not assert binding to all receptor types.

Below y=800: a large sage intracellular receptor in cytoplasm at x=220,y=1030, visibly binding the entering diamond. Label "Internal receptor" in two lines. At x=690,y=1120 draw a generous completely enclosed nucleus whose whole outline fits INSIDE the image, clear double-line nuclear envelope, large label "Nucleus". Inside it show a short DNA ribbon with a receptor-associated region and label "Gene regulation". A dashed route from the cytoplasmic receptor goes through one recognizable nuclear pore to the DNA-associated region. This is a simplified receptor/transcription route, not a literal universal trafficking claim. Intracellular receptors need not remain exclusively in the nucleus. No other organelles or extra membrane bands.

Exact allowed labels only: "Where can the signal reach?", "Outside", "Inside", "Cell membrane", "Ion channel", "GPCR", "Enzyme-linked", "Ion flow", "G protein", "Kinase example", "Stays outside", "Can enter", "Internal receptor", "Nucleus", "Gene regulation", "P". No Greek letter labels. No other prose. Avoid tiny typography, stock people, faces, glossy glowing rendering, logos and watermarks. Diagram not to molecular scale; these families are a selection, not an exhaustive taxonomy. Channel opening is a chosen state, not guaranteed by binding. Kinase is one enzyme-linked example; other enzyme-linked receptors rely on associated enzymes. Surface access does not prove growth-driving kinase or benefit. Do not copy a source figure.

Light theme: warm ivory background, dark navy labels and outlines, soft muted teal membrane, slate-blue channel and GPCR, sand and muted ochre enzyme example, dusty violet nucleus, sage internal receptor, coral ligands and probe. Calm colors and readable contrast, no glowing effects. Maintain gentle paper texture and clear silhouette boundaries.
